summary: The subclass and model-split direction matches existing patterns, but the brief assumes several extension points that the current implementation does not actually provide. The main risks are configuration isolation, JSON-2 method coverage, inherited tool exposure, and unsafe or unverifiable transition behavior.

suggestions.title: Make known-model registration polymorphic
suggestions.rationale: `list_models()` iterates the module-level `_DEFAULT_KNOWN_MODELS`; assigning an override on `OdooHelpdeskToolkit` will have no effect. Either make the constant a class attribute used through `self`, or override `list_models()` explicitly and test that helpdesk models appear.

suggestions.title: Prevent helpdesk credentials from falling through to generic Odoo credentials
suggestions.rationale: `OdooToolkit.__init__` resolves every value with `value or ODOO_*`, so an intentionally empty helpdesk database can fall back to `ODOO_DATABASE`; the same applies to URL, user, and password. Adding new config constants alone does not isolate tenants. Use explicit `is not None` resolution or a config/transport injection seam, and test empty-database plus conflicting-environment cases.

suggestions.title: Do not expose unrestricted inherited CRUD by default
suggestions.rationale: Reflection scans every public async method, so the subclass inherits generic create/update/delete, shell, diagnostics, and arbitrary-model operations. `odoo.write`/`odoo.delete` are framework permissions, not helpdesk record or field restrictions. A helpdesk agent could mutate or delete unrelated ERP records. Define an explicitly safe tool profile with `exclude_tools` or composition, or require a separate administrator-facing toolkit.

suggestions.title: Choose a distinct prefix when both toolkits may coexist
suggestions.rationale: Both classes would expose the same inherited `odoo_*` names. The tool manager treats collisions from prefixed toolkits as hard errors, so loading `OdooToolkit` and `OdooHelpdeskToolkit` together fails rather than merely shadowing one. Resolve the deployment model and test registration with both instances; `odoo_hd` is the safer default if coexistence is expected.

suggestions.title: Add an explicit JSON-2 mapping for name resolution
suggestions.rationale: The current JSON-2 mapper handles search, search_read, search_count, read, create, write, unlink, fields_get, and load, but has no `name_search` branch. The generic fallback rejects the usual multiple positional arguments. Any create/reference helper promising id-or-name resolution must use `search_read` deliberately or add and test a named-argument mapping.

suggestions.title: Treat wizard calls as transport-specific contracts
suggestions.rationale: The JSON-2 fallback only supports no positional arguments or one positional id list. Reassign, merge, and mass-update wizard flows commonly require additional positional values or multi-step context, which will fail before reaching Odoo. Verify each exact method signature and either encode named JSON-2 mappings or exclude unsupported wizard operations from the JSON-2 v1 surface.

suggestions.title: Do not silently convert action failure into direct stage writes
suggestions.rationale: The existing action-then-read-back precedent invokes the action and reads the record, but does not detect wizard returns, no-ops, or unchanged state. A fallback `stage_id` write can bypass notifications, SLA recomputation, audit logic, and invariants. Require an expected current stage, verify the postcondition, return the raw action/warning state, and make any direct-write fallback an explicit operation with separate tests.

suggestions.title: Normalize derived helpdesk output before Pydantic validation
suggestions.rationale: Existing entities mostly mirror Odoo wire fields under `_OdooEntity(extra='allow')`; there is no established transformation for turning one2many `extra_field_ids` records into `dict[str, str]` or deriving a lifecycle block from `stage_id` and boolean fields. Define a normalization boundary or validators, preserve the raw values, and test missing, false, list, and malformed custom-field shapes.

suggestions.title: Constrain ticket write payloads instead of forwarding arbitrary dictionaries
suggestions.rationale: The existing generic write input accepts `dict[str, Any]`, while the proposed ticket tools include lifecycle, assignment, SLA, and tenant-specific fields with materially different safety semantics. A typed `update_ticket` that merely forwards an arbitrary dict is an unbounded escape hatch. Use explicit patch fields and separate privileged/raw operations; validate writable fields against `fields_get` and reject stage/SLA changes outside transition tools.

suggestions.title: Union helpdesk HITL rules with inherited confirmation rules
suggestions.rationale: `confirming_tools` is a class attribute, and the base currently protects shell install/upgrade/CLI tools. Replacing it on the subclass with cancel/merge/mass-update names would remove the inherited shell confirmations. Build the subclass set as the union with `OdooToolkit.confirming_tools` and assert both inherited and new destructive tools retain confirmation metadata.

suggestions.title: Test stable stats envelopes across Odoo 19 and legacy result shapes
suggestions.rationale: The aggregate tool currently returns Odoo groups verbatim, and FEAT-614 explicitly preserves the differing `formatted_read_group` versus `read_group` shapes. A typed `TicketStatsResult` that assumes one shape will be transport/version dependent. Add fixtures for both responses and normalize counts/group keys at the helpdesk boundary, with no-live-network unit coverage.
